# SF_Experience_Cloud — review deck

**Generated by `python scripts/vault.py cards`. Do not edit the cards here —
edit the `## Recall` block in the note they came from.** Scheduling comments
written by the spaced-repetition plugin are preserved across regenerations.

Which Experience Cloud templates are LWR-based?
?
Only two — Build Your Own (LWR) and Microsite (LWR). Customer Service, Partner Central, Customer Account Portal, Help Center and Build Your Own are Aura.

Have Aura templates been retired?
?
No. They are legacy in direction only — still creatable at 67.0, still receiving Summer '26 features, with no announced retirement date.

What does choosing LWR cost you on a self-service portal project?
?
Everything Customer Service gave you for free — Knowledge, case deflection, feed and search all become build work on a blank canvas.

Can Aura components run in an LWR site?
?
No. LWR runs Lightning web components only, and there is no compatibility layer.

What is the structural gap in LWR that surprises Aura developers?
?
No generic record pages — record components only work on object-specific pages — plus a 500-route cap per site.

What single fact explains LWR's caching, SEO and component rules?
?
An LWR site is built at publish time into static, immutable, cacheable assets and served from a CDN — it is not rendered per request.

Which metadata types distinguish enhanced LWR from non-enhanced?
?
Enhanced uses `DigitalExperienceBundle` and `DigitalExperienceConfig`; non-enhanced LWR — like Aura — uses `ExperienceBundle`.

Is the Upgrade to Enhanced LWR Sites Release Update enforced?
?
No. Available Spring '25 and scheduled for Spring '26, but not enforced since Summer '25 — it is a recommendation.

What is the status and scope of Experience Delivery?
?
**Discontinued as of Winter '27.** It was the Cloudflare-backed hosting tier — Beta from Summer '24, Build Your Own (LWR) only, Enterprise/Performance/Unlimited, no Developer Edition. Republishing migrates a site to standard LWR infrastructure.

Did SSR go away with Experience Delivery?
?
No. Islands SSR is a standard LWR Experience Cloud capability and is on by default on Build Your Own (LWR) standard pages. Experience Delivery was the hosting tier, not the rendering model.

What switches SSR on for an LWR page, and what turns it off by accident?
?
The theme layout's `lightning__ServerRenderable` capability. A custom theme layout that omits it makes the entire route client-rendered, silently.

Which two setup decisions in Experience Cloud are permanent?
?
The org's Digital Experiences domain name, and each site's URL prefix — plus the template's runtime, decided at creation.

What is the difference between publishing and activating a site?
?
Publish makes Experience Builder changes live; activate makes the site reachable by members. They are independent.

Which CDN serves an Experience Delivery site?
?
Cloudflare — the default Salesforce CDN path for other Experience Cloud domains is Akamai. Experience Delivery itself is discontinued as of Winter '27, so Cloudflare's remaining Experience Cloud case is Commerce LWR.

What happens when a site is set to Inactive?
?
It serves the customisable Service Not Available page; the published assets are unaffected.

Why is the end of My Domain redirections an Experience Cloud problem specifically?
?
Guest site URLs are the most widely linked-to URLs an org owns, so stale hostnames now 404 for external people you cannot reach.

What is the difference between a theme layout and a page layout in Experience Builder?
?
The theme layout is site-wide chrome around every page; the page layout divides one page's body into regions.

Which targets make an LWC usable as LWR chrome and as page structure?
?
`lightningCommunity__Theme_Layout` and `lightningCommunity__Page_Layout` respectively.

How do you create a droppable region inside a custom LWR layout?
?
With slots — a default `<slot>` for main content in a theme layout, named slots for regions in a page layout.

Why is a custom theme layout's property not editable in Experience Builder?
?
Because the theme layout target doesn't support properties on its own; `lightningCommunity__Default` must be added with the properties in `targetConfigs`.

Which visibility mechanism requires enhanced LWR?
?
Expression-based visibility — non-enhanced LWR sites get component-level visibility rules only.

What does a theme layout decide besides chrome?
?
Whether the page is server-rendered. Without the `lightning__ServerRenderable` capability on the theme layout, the whole route is client-rendered.

What is the `--dxp-*` custom property system for?
?
LWR's reduced set of styling hooks that map onto lower-level component hooks, so one value brands many components at once.

What happened to standard design tokens under SLDS 2?
?
They aren't included — SLDS 2 replaces them with global styling hooks, so token-branded sites lose their branding rather than change it.

Which styling hooks are portable across SLDS 1 and SLDS 2?
?
The global `--slds-g-*` hooks. Component-level `--slds-c-*` hooks are not supported in SLDS 2.

What is a branding set?
?
A named, switchable collection of a site's branding property values — the mechanism for sub-brands and seasonal skins within one site.

Why can't you brand a component by overriding its CSS classes?
?
Shadow DOM scopes styles, so selectors don't reach in. Custom properties do, which is why the whole system is built on them.

Which target makes a component's properties editable in Experience Builder?
?
`lightningCommunity__Default`, declared alongside the target that exposes the component.

When does a managed-package LWC actually need `lightningCommunity__RelaxedCSP`?
?
Only on sites running with Lightning Locker / LWS off. It is a capability, not a target, and it is not required on a normal Locker-on LWR site.

Why does `ShowToastEvent` do nothing in an LWR site?
?
It's a bubbling event that needs a Lightning Experience container. Use `lightning/toast` with `lightning/toastContainer`.

What are the two constraints on code that runs during SSR?
?
It must be portable — no browser APIs — and synchronous. So no async work in `connectedCallback()` or getters.

How does a component detect that it's running on the server?
?
The `import.meta.env.SSR` boolean is true during server-side rendering and falsy on the client.

Is a guest-facing `@AuraEnabled` method protected by the component in front of it?
?
No. It's an endpoint; its own checks are the boundary — and a pre-67.0 class isn't enforcing the access model at all.

What is the only way to grant an unauthenticated guest access to a record?
?
A guest user sharing rule — criteria-based, Read Only, 50 per object. Nothing else grants a guest record access.

Can a guest user own a record?
?
No. Records created by guests are assigned to a default owner, and the setting enforcing this can't be turned off.

Which object permissions can a guest user hold?
?
Read and create only. Edit, delete, View All Records and Modify All Records cannot be granted, even via a permission set.

What replaced the `View All Users` permission for guests?
?
The per-site *Let guest users see other members of this site* setting; the permission was removed from all guests in Winter '21.

Was the 2026 Experience Cloud campaign a platform vulnerability?
?
No — it exploited over-permissive guest configurations that predated the 2020–21 hardening.

Which distinction between external licences matters most architecturally?
?
High-volume versus role-based. High-volume users have no role, so the role hierarchy, sharing rules and manual sharing don't apply to them.

Which licences give an external user a role?
?
Customer Community Plus, Partner Community and External Apps. Customer Community is high-volume and role-less.

What does a guest user consume from the licence pool?
?
Nothing — unauthenticated visitors use no external licence, which is why guest access is controlled separately.

What is the difference between member-based and login-based licensing?
?
A billing metric only. Member-based is a provisioned seat; login-based draws from a monthly login pool. Sporadic use favours login-based.

What does super user access grant, and to whom?
?
To Partner and Customer Community Plus users — visibility of records created by others in their account at or below their role, for Cases, Leads, Opportunities and custom objects.

Why can't sharing rules grant access to a Customer Community user?
?
High-volume users have no role. Sharing rules grant to groups, roles and territories, none of which can name a role-less user.

What does a sharing set actually match on?
?
A lookup on the target object resolving to the user's own Contact or Account — access by relationship, not by group membership.

What problem does a share group solve?
?
Records owned by high-volume external users are invisible to internal staff; a share group grants named users access to them.

Which external users use the ordinary sharing mechanisms?
?
Role-based ones — Customer Community Plus, Partner Community and External Apps — whose roles sit under the account owner in the hierarchy.

What breaks about "Roles and Subordinates" in an org with a portal?
?
It includes portal and community roles. Use the *Internal* variant unless external inheritance is intended.

Where is Experience Cloud login configured?
?
Per site, in the Login & Registration workspace — identity providers, self-registration, forgot password and user creation behaviour.

What is the difference between self-registration and JIT provisioning?
?
Self-registration creates the user from a Salesforce-hosted form; JIT creates them from an external IdP's assertion on first federated login.

What does a login flow sit between?
?
Accepted credentials and a granted session — which is why an error in one locks every user out.

What is Headless Identity for?
?
Letting an off-platform front end own the entire login, registration and password-reset UI while Salesforce remains the authentication authority.

Does the 2026 phishing-resistant MFA requirement apply to portal users?
?
No — it targets privileged internal access. It reaches an Experience Cloud project through the admins who run the site, not its external users.

What is the single highest-value item to remove from a guest profile?
?
`API Enabled` — with it, the site is a queryable data surface rather than a set of pages.

Why is "we hardened it at launch" not an acceptable answer?
?
Schema and permission changes widen the guest surface over time, so exposure is a standing audit item, not a one-off task.

Was the March 2026 Experience Cloud campaign a platform vulnerability?
?
No. Salesforce's advisory is explicit that it exploited over-permissive customer configurations, not a platform defect.

Which sites need auditing?
?
All of them, including inactive and preview sites — each has its own guest user, and preview status restricts membership, not reachability.

What protects data behind a guest-facing `@AuraEnabled` method?
?
Only that class's own enforcement. A class below API 67.0, or one in system mode, isn't applying the access model at all.

Is there a supported converter from an Aura Experience Cloud site to LWR?
?
No. The path is a rebuild in a new site followed by a cutover; the runtimes share only the builder.

What is the false premise behind most Aura-to-LWR migration business cases?
?
That Aura templates are retired or dated. They aren't — they have no announced end-of-life and still received features in Summer '26.

What actually carries across from the old site?
?
Apex logic and CMS content. Components, layouts and CSS do not.

Which kind of site gets a genuine return from LWR?
?
A public, guest-heavy, SEO-relevant one, where the build-and-cache model pays. A logged-in partner portal on Partner Central usually doesn't.

What is the commonly missed cutover risk?
?
URLs — the new site must take over the custom domain and paths, and old indexed or bookmarked links need deliberate redirection.

What are the three grains an audience can target in an LWR site?
?
A whole page variation, an individual component's visibility, and which navigation menu is assigned.

Why does hiding a navigation item not secure a page?
?
The audience rule hides the link, but the page's URL is still directly reachable — access must be enforced by guest sharing and page-level rules.

What determines whether a record type appears in site search results?
?
It must be a searchable object for the site *and* the running (or guest) user must have sharing visibility to the record.

When two audiences both match a visitor, which applies?
?
The first matching audience in order — ordering shadows narrower rules placed below broad ones.

What new audience criteria did enhanced LWR sites add?
?
Record-based and CMS-content-based criteria, enabling content-driven personalization rather than only user attributes.

What is the relationship between a CMS workspace and a channel?
?
Many-to-many — a workspace publishes to multiple channels, and a channel can draw from multiple enhanced workspaces. It decouples authoring from delivery.

How do you create a custom content type programmatically, and what's the cap?
?
Via Metadata API (`ManagedContentType`) or Tooling API (`ManagedContentNodeType`); up to 100 active custom types org-wide.

What are the collection limits?
?
A manual collection holds **50 items** of a single content type; a dynamic, query-driven collection returns up to **250**, by relevance. Both tiers are capped — quote them together.

What changed with "enhanced" CMS workspaces, and since when?
?
Since Winter '25 new workspaces are enhanced by default, adding cross-workspace sharing, variants, folders and org-wide taxonomy tags. Classic workspaces are the migration source.

Which site runtime does Enhanced CMS assume, and why does it matter?
?
Enhanced LWR (distinct from plain LWR) — the wrong runtime won't get the full enhanced-delivery surface, so verify the site's runtime before designing around it.

Does a headless implementation still require an Experience Cloud site?
?
Yes — Headless Identity APIs and the guest/licensing context are exposed through a site even when no Experience Builder pages are rendered.

Where is Headless Identity covered, and should this note restate it?
?
In [10 · Authentication](10-authentication-self-registration-and-sso.md) — this note cross-links it rather than restating the login/registration/passwordless flows.

What do you give up by going headless that Experience Builder gave you for free?
?
The static build, the CDN, the auto-generated sitemap, per-page meta — and the platform's islands SSR, which survived Experience Delivery's discontinuation. You own caching, SEO and server rendering yourself.

What is the main judgment call for choosing headless?
?
Bespoke UX / native app / external design system versus Experience Builder's faster launch and admin maintainability — pick headless only when UX control genuinely outweighs those.

As which user do a public headless front end's data calls execute?
?
The guest user — so the guest exposure audit and sharing rules govern every exposed endpoint.

What single architectural fact explains LWR's caching, SEO and SSR-safe rules?
?
LWR sites are built and served from a CDN, not rendered per request like Aura.

What is the status of Experience Delivery, and what did it actually take with it?
?
**Discontinued as of Winter '27**; republishing migrates the site to standard LWR infrastructure. It was the Cloudflare hosting and edge tier — it did *not* take server-side rendering, which remains a standard LWR capability.

What breaks server-side rendering (and the build) in a custom component?
?
Touching `window`/`document` at module scope — guard browser-only code with `import.meta.env.SSR` and defer it to a lifecycle hook.

What does LWR give you for SEO?
?
Server-rendered HTML on SSR-enabled pages, an auto-generated sitemap, clean URLs, and per-page meta/Open Graph tags.

When does a content change actually reach visitors?
?
At publish, when the static build regenerates and propagates to the CDN — not on save.

What does Mobile Publisher produce, and how is it licensed?
?
A branded native iOS/Android app with its own store listing, push and biometric login — licensed per app, submitted through your own Apple/Google developer accounts.

Which changes to a Mobile Publisher app require store resubmission, and which don't?
?
Native/branding (binary) changes require resubmission; content published to the underlying live site appears without it, since the app loads the live site.

What's the core trade between Mobile Publisher and a PWA?
?
Native app buys store presence, push and device APIs at the cost of review and resubmission; PWA buys instant updates and no store friction at the cost of native reach and discoverability.

Who reviews and approves a Mobile Publisher app?
?
Apple and Google — it's a store review, not a Salesforce approval, so build in lead time and rejection risk.

Why might a simple portal be rejected from the App Store?
?
Store guidelines can reject thin "just a website" apps or login-walled content lacking native value.

Which metadata type does a modern (enhanced) LWR site use?
?
`DigitalExperienceBundle` (with `DigitalExperienceConfig`) — plain-text and diffable, and *not* retrievable under `ExperienceBundle`.

Does `ExperienceBundle` tell you the site's runtime?
?
No — Aura and non-enhanced LWR sites both use it, so it identifies diffability, not the runtime.

Why is `SiteDotCom` a source-control dead end?
?
It's a binary blob Salesforce regenerates differently on every retrieve, so diffs never show meaningful changes.

What's the silent failure when your manifest names the wrong site metadata type?
?
The retrieve/deploy finds nothing for that site — no error, the site simply doesn't come across.

Does deploying a site's metadata make changes visible to visitors?
?
No — the site must still be published; deploy updates the definition, publish serves it.

What is the deployment chain for putting a chat or agent on a site?
?
Messaging Channel (In-App and Web) → Embedded Service Deployment → Embedded Messaging component in Experience Builder → publish.

What is the product called, and what happened to the one before it?
?
**Enhanced Chat** — renamed from *Messaging for In-App and Web* in June 2025, with **v2** since Winter '26. Legacy Chat / Live Agent **was retired on 14 February 2026**.

How does the site know whether a conversation goes to a human or an agent?
?
It doesn't — the channel routes via Omni-Channel to a queue or an Agentforce Service Agent; routing is configured behind the channel.

Why is an agent on a public site the highest-risk deployment surface?
?
It combines unauthenticated input, guest-user data context, and a reasoning engine — so prompt injection and over-broad actions can exfiltrate data.

As which user does a public-site agent operate, and what does that bound?
?
The guest user — its data reach and every action are limited to guest sharing, so the guest profile and agent actions must both be tightly scoped.

Where does an embedded agent belong on the exposure audit?
?
It's a new line item on the public-site exposure audit ([11](11-public-site-exposure-audit.md)) — not a separate subject — plus the Trust Layer controls.

What does an Experience Cloud site primarily meter on, and at what allowance?
?
Page views, monthly and per edition — **Enterprise 500,000/month**, **Unlimited and Performance 1,000,000/month** — not the number of users.

What happens when a site exceeds its page-view allowance?
?
More than a bill. At **110% for four consecutive calendar months**, or **300% in a single month**, Salesforce can **disable the sites** until the next month or until more page views are purchased — so an unmodeled viral launch is an availability risk as well as a cost one.

What's the org-wide site-count cap, and what counts against it?
?
100 sites per org, including inactive, preview and Visualforce sites — so dead experiments consume headroom.

Are API limits per user or per org?
?
Per org — an aggregate 24-hour allocation shared across every integration and headless client.

What is guest throttling for, and what's the blunt lever?
?
To blunt scraping/abuse — you can rate-limit and fully disable guest API access via the site setting plus the guest profile's `API Enabled` permission.

Does a Salesforce Accessibility Conformance Report make your Experience Cloud site conformant?
?
No. It describes Salesforce's components. A regulator looks at the rendered page — template, branding set, content, custom components — and the obligation sits with the service provider.

Which WCAG version binds under the European Accessibility Act?
?
WCAG 2.1 AA, via EN 301 549 v3.2.1 — the version cited in the Official Journal. v4.1.1 (WCAG 2.2) was published 2 September 2026 but is not yet cited, so it confers no presumption of conformity.

Which ACR covers your site, and what decides it?
?
The runtime, fixed by the template. *Experience Cloud – LWR* covers Build Your Own (LWR) and Microsite (LWR); *Experience Cloud – Aura* covers Customer Service, Customer Account Portal and Partner Central.

What does the EAA require beyond an accessible site?
?
A statement — Art. 13(2) and Annex V — in the general terms, in accessible written and oral form, explaining how the service meets the requirements and kept current for the life of the service.

Where do an LWR site's F6 navigation regions come from?
?
Slots in the theme layout. A custom theme layout that drops them loses the regions with no error.
